260ade897e427c1f: BEIJING: Human actors in China are getting a much-needed lifeline as authorities move to protect traditional television and digital media from an overwhelming flood of artificial intelligence.
China's National Radio and Television Administration (NRTA) has promised direct financial support for live-action productions, according to 8Days.
The goal is to safeguard authentic storytelling and keep real actors in work amid an unprecedented boom in AI-generated content.
The sheer volume of synthetic media hitting screens has been staggering.

According to Wang Xiaoliang, director at the NRTA's Department of Online Audio-Visual Programme Management, around 430,000 micro-dramas were released in China during the first eight months of 2026 alone. That is a 13-fold jump compared to the whole of last year. Over 90 per cent of these releases were created using AI.
While quick turnaround times and tiny production budgets have made synthetic shows immensely popular, human performers are paying the price.
Actors face severe financial fallout, drastic pay cuts, and acute job scarcity.
Some have even resorted to licensing their faces and voices to AI production companies for as little as 100 yuan (about RM60.80).
In response, regulators are stepping in to protect talent and boost production values.
"Our position is very clear: live-action dramas are the main force behind quality productions and should receive strong support," Wang said at a recent press conference.
He confirmed plans to "put real money" into these projects so compelling stories can secure distribution and financial returns.

Alongside funding, digital platforms face stricter rules. Under regulations that took effect on Sept 1, AI-generated micro-dramas must clearly display labels stating their synthetic origin, respect image and voice rights, and follow updated compliance standards.
Authorities have already pulled 68,000 micro-dramas for copyright infringement, piracy, and inappropriate content—with over 90 per cent of the flagged shows coming from AI.
The crackdown has sparked lively debate online. Supporters argue that human actors bring irreplaceable emotional depth and warmth to the screen.
Critics, however, question whether funding traditional formats will do much to change shifting audience tastes.
While AI offers speed and convenience, Wang maintains that ethics and creative integrity must come first.
"AI is a tool; people are the creators," he said, proving that human storytellers will not be replaced so easily.

TANJUNG MALIM: Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) graduates must go beyond mastering technical skills and be equipped to harness artificial intelligence (AI), drive innovation and build their own businesses.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said this would be driven by three priorities aimed at taking TVET graduates further in skills mastery, innovation and entrepreneurship.
"Mastery of AI, data and digital technology must become a core competency of graduates.
"This mastery must be accompanied by the ability to solve problems, communicate and make ethical judgements.

"We want graduates to know how to use technology effectively while remaining courteous and responsible," he said in his speech at the Central Zone Polytechnic and Community College Convocation Ceremony at Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris here today.
Zahid said the second priority was for the Polytechnic and Community College Education Department (POLYCC) to strengthen applied innovation in collaboration with industry.
He said promising projects should be tested in real-world conditions, improved and eventually brought to market.
"For example, a smart irrigation system developed by students could be tested with farmers to reduce water wastage and make their work easier.
"This is where institutions and industry need to provide guidance and pathways towards commercialisation," he said.
On the third priority, Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development minister said more pathways should be created for graduates to build their own businesses.
He cited Ampang Community College graduate Noor Azree Aiman, who founded ASZR Legacy in the mobile phone repair sector.
"With skills and entrepreneurial guidance, he expanded his business by opening two more branches and creating employment opportunities for local youths," he said.
Zahid said such examples demonstrated the potential to move graduates beyond skills mastery towards building businesses and creating opportunities for others.
"We are proud of Made in Malaysia and we want to go further by making it Made by Malaysians," he said.
He said polyCC's network of 23,580 industry partners should also be translated into deeper involvement in curriculum development, industrial training and professional certification.
"Industry needs to work with us from the outset in developing the talent they require, including providing exposure to the latest technologies and workplace practices," he said.
Zahid said expertise should also be developed based on the strengths of individual institutions.

He cited Sultan Nazrin Shah Maritime Polytechnic, which he wanted to see further strengthened as a strategic maritime TVET institution, with training and certification that met industry needs and international standards.
He also called for the success of 55 polytechnic graduates who completed training at Liuzhou Railway Vocational Technical College in China on Sept 5 to be expanded across polyCC.
"Such exposure needs to be broadened so that graduates can master technology and gain international experience," he said.

922cd8b6fcda3aa0: SAN SEBASTIAN (Spain), Sept 24 — Hollywood star Brad Pitt said yesterday that co-starring with a dog in his latest film, survival thriller Heart of the Beast, was “a really moving experience”.
Directed by David Ayer, the film explores the deep bond between a military officer and his combat dog, Odin, who survive an air crash and become trapped in the wilderness of Alaska.
Four dogs, all from the same family, were used to portray Odin, but the bulk of the performance was delivered by a German shepherd named Uber.

“I did have a really moving experience with Uber who plays Odin, who our dog whisperer found in New Zealand, and we bonded quickly,” Pitt told a news conference at Spain’s San Sebastian Film Festival, where the movie is screening out of competition.

“There were times he would do things that were just amazing, that were not in the script that you see in the film, and his expressions, they really moved me with him in the close-up,” the 62-year-old Oscar winner added.
San Sebastian, the highest-profile film festival in the Spanish-speaking world, wraps up on Saturday.
A total of 17 films are vying for the top awards in the official section, with a jury presided over by US director Ira Sachs. — AFP
18a3548511582623: KUALA LUMPUR: Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing has called on police to conduct a thorough investigation into a series of attacks targeting 24-hour convenience stores in several parts of Sarawak.

Tiong said the incidents, involving suspected explosive or flammable objects, arson and vandalism, should be investigated collectively across districts to determine whether they were linked and identify those responsible, including anyone who may have planned or ordered the attacks.
He said the incidents were reported in Kuching, Sri Aman and Bintulu, with outlets of the same convenience store chain targeted within 24 hours.
"It is especially alarming that some of the incidents took place while people were still inside the premises.
"Knowing that there were people inside and still throwing dangerous objects into the shop is a blatant disregard for the law and for human lives," he said in a post on Facebook.
Tiong said such acts of intimidation, arson, violence and conduct that endangered lives should not be allowed to take root in Sarawak.

He also called on the police to establish who planned and carried out the attacks, the motive for targeting the stores, whether anyone had directed the perpetrators and whether the incidents involved an organised operation.
"If this is not stopped quickly, what meaning does the law have?" he said.
Tiong said the investigation should go beyond those who carried out the attacks to determine whether there were others who planned or ordered them.
"If others planned or ordered it, the real masterminds must not be allowed to escape responsibility," he said.
He also urged authorities not to allow disputes or allegations to be settled through violence or intimidation, stressing that any dispute should be dealt with through legal channels.
"We must put a stop to gangster-style violence. Violence and intimidation cannot become a way to settle problems.
"We cannot wait until someone loses their life before taking action," he said.
22e23bebe50134ce: NEW YORK: Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan began his engagements on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) with a courtesy call from Commonwealth Secretary-General Shirley Botchwey.

The meeting focused on the Commonwealth's future direction in addressing global challenges and preparations for the 28th Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda in November.
In a statement, Mohamad and Shirley also discussed challenges facing the Commonwealth, including democracy, the rule of law and human rights.
"In this regard, Malaysia continues to be entrusted as a member of the Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group to uphold the values and principles of the Commonwealth.
"Malaysia has been a member of CMAG since 2018," it said in a statement to BuletinTV3.
Mohamad will represent Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim at CHOGM, which will also focus on trade and investment opportunities.

Malaysia also welcomed the expansion of the Commonwealth's network of relations, including with Bahrain, Brazil, Kuwait, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, which have been invited to attend CHOGM for the first time.
Tomorrow, Mohamad is scheduled to attend several high-level ministerial meetings at the United Nations headquarters.
He will attend the Ministerial Meeting of the Peacebuilding Commission at the Trusteeship Council Chamber, where Malaysia is 34th in line to deliver its statement.
This will be followed by the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation Annual Coordination Meeting for Foreign Ministers, where Malaysia is scheduled to speak after Kyrgyzstan and before Sierra Leone.
He will then attend the Ministerial Meeting in Support of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees 2026 at the Economic and Social Council Chamber.
Mohamad is also scheduled to meet Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide.
He will then participate in the High-Level Meeting on Addressing the Existential Threats Posed by Sea-Level Rise, where Malaysia is 61st in line to deliver its statement.
He will conclude the programme by receiving a courtesy call from International Committee of the Red Cross president Mirjana Spoljaric Egger at the UN headquarters.
Mohamad is in New York from Sept 23 to 27 to lead the Malaysian delegation to the 81st UNGA.

b97f46a3a80c384e: TOKYO: China's 13-year-old swimming prodigy Yu Zidi has stamped her mark all over the Asian Games and she could cause a sensation at the Los Angeles Olympics in two years' time.
The schoolgirl won all three individual races she swam this week in Tokyo with Asian Games records — a series of performances that belied her tender age.
Out of the pool she proved herself to be a typical teenager, joking around with team-mates and freezing when asked about herself in interviews.
She will be 15 when the LA Olympics come round in 2028 and likely to be a major medal threat with the world watching.
"She hasn't become that fast for no reason," said team-mate Ke Wenxi, who Yu beat in the 400m individual medley final to complete her golden hat-trick.
"I've seen how hard she works in training. During this national team training camp, I saw her working really hard every day."
Yu also won the 200m butterfly and 200m individual medley races this week in Tokyo.
Her times were among the fastest in the world this year and her 200m medley swim was just 0.4sec off the world record.
That mark is held by Canada's Summer McIntosh, who is likely to be Yu's biggest rival at the LA Games.
Yu would not be drawn on her ambitions for the Olympics, saying only that she intended to "keep working hard."
It hinted at a mature attitude and a desire not to be shaken off in her pursuit of success.
"I gained a lot from these Asian Games but there were also some regrets," she said.
"I'll go back and keep reviewing what I didn't do well, and I hope I can do better next time."
- Room for two -
As might be expected of someone who does not turn 14 until next month, Yu was less comfortable out of the pool than in it.
She complained that "interviews are way harder than the race", openly admitting that she struggles in front of large numbers of reporters.
"How do I answer this question? Can you teach me? You just want me to say what I feel?" she said after one question.
When asked if competing this week had been easy, Yu stared in wide-eyed amazement for several seconds before replying: "Definitely not."
She has seemed most at ease in the company of her team-mates, especially 15-year-old Ke.
Yu and Ke, who shared a room in Tokyo, made heart signs and chatted happily together as they celebrated their one-two finish in the 400m medley.
"There are three beds in our room – two are pushed together to make a big bed, and there is another smaller one," said Ke.
"I let her have the bigger bed because the smaller one was enough for me.
"I wanted her to have somewhere more comfortable to sleep."
Yu has spoken in the past about struggling to deal with the heavy load placed on her.
She was discovered by a swimming coach while at a water park aged six and since then has juggled schoolwork with training.
"Being in class all day and still having to train was really tiring," she said in January.
She called her Asian Games experience "challenging" and things are not likely to get any easier on the road to the Olympics.
If she can maintain her focus, she could be one of the stars of the Games.
"I don't think about anything else," she said when asked about what she thinks about before a race.
"I just think about the little details and my movements."

eae531704d6d3d78: TOWNSVILLE: Carlo Ancelotti's Brazil and hosts Australia will use their friendly double-header as the first stage of a rebuilding process following the World Cup.
Brazil take on the Socceroos in Townsville on Friday before a second clash in Brisbane next Tuesday.
It will be both countries' first outings since their World Cup campaigns ended in July.
The Socceroos bowed out in the round of 32 while five-time champions Brazil suffered a shock loss to Norway in the last 16.
Brazil coach Ancelotti has responded by selecting only nine players from their World Cup squad for the two Australian matches and a friendly against India in Kolkata on October 3.

Chelsea forwards Joao Pedro and Estevao were recalled, while Ancelotti has included several new faces, among them goalkeepers Pedro Morisco and Otavio, defender Mauro Junior, and midfielders Breno Bidon and Gabriel Bontempo.
Several of Brazil's established stars will be in action, including forwards Vinicius Junior and Raphinha, Arsenal midfielder Bruno Guimaraes and central defenders Gabriel Magalhaes and Marquinhos.
Guimaraes said this week that it was important that new faces had been included.
"We are constantly refining talent in our country," he said.
"It's crucial to have that solid foundation, so the coach can keep discovering new talent.
"Of course we respect Australia and hope we have a great game," he added.
"Things haven't been great recently, but from my perspective, the only way to turn the situation around is by playing well and winning games."

Australian coach Tony Popovic also swung the selection axe, omitting 10 players from the Socceroos' World Cup squad, including veteran goalkeeper and captain Mat Ryan, and striker Cristian Volpato, who was fined this month after testing positive for cocaine.
Popovic named seven uncapped players in the 25-man squad, which was rocked by the injury-forced withdrawal of in-form Norwich City striker Mohamed Toure.
Australia are building towards the Asian Cup in January-February.
Experienced midfielder Jackson Irvine said the two Brazil matches were a good chance for new players to prove themselves on a big stage.
"I think it's a really exciting one for us, to come off the back of the World Cup and progress even further with our football, with new players, a chance to take the next step again," he said.
"We need to take another step.
"We did amazing things over the summer, but we've got another tournament coming and for us to grow, we have to look to progress." - AFP

70b12340875a76ce: HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for an ethics-driven approach to artificial intelligence (AI) and a more open, rules-based digital trade regime to ensure developing nations share in the gains of technological progress.

Speaking at the opening ceremony of the 5th Global Digital Trade Expo here, he acknowledged China’s advancement in visualisation and AI as well as its role in sharing technological advancements with the Global South.
“To my mind, this is what is remarkable about the Chinese leadership, and their willingness to continue to give meaning and essence to real globalisation,” he said in his keynote address here.
Held at the Hangzhou Grand Convention and Exhibition Centre, the five-day expo officiated by China’s Premier Li Qiang is one of China’s major digital economy platforms.

Anwar, who is also the finance ninister, said Malaysia’s objectives in AI are clear, namely to raise productivity, help smaller firms compete, and move industries into higher-value work, while ensuring that Malaysians gain from technological change rather than merely live with its consequences.

“The principle remains, either we govern artificial intelligence or artificial intelligence will govern us,” he said, while calling for an ethics-based framework to ensure that innovation and technological advancement remain firmly in the service of humanity

He said this was a fundamental issue that touched on the recurring problem of the digital divide, particularly as nations pursued rapid technological advancement amid persistent socio-economic inequalities.

“Exponential growth of AI, for example, may be what most nations aspire to, but what purpose would it really serve humanity if such expansion only leads to widening the gap between wealthy and developing nations, advanced and developing economies?

“This is not an imagined or exaggerated fear but a profound concern for the well-being of regions, nations, and communities. The question is whether these technologies will give developing countries a larger say in their own future or leave them dependent on technologies designed elsewhere,” he said.
Anwar said true economic advancement could not proceed in a vacuum, while real expansion of technology could not be sustained without considering the technology gap.
The Prime Minister’s three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou concludes today.

China has remained Malaysia’s largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, with total bilateral trade reaching US$113.82 billion (RM456.68 billion) between January and August this year. — Bernama

0960ff02a457ead6: LETTERS: I remember 2002 vividly. I had just joined the Asean Secretariat in Jakarta when the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution was signed with great fanfare.

It was hailed as a landmark regional commitment to prevent and control the haze. Yet, over two decades later, the choking smog continues to return, accompanied each time by familiar statements, diplomatic meetings and renewed calls for "cooperation".
Singapore took a decisive step by enacting its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act, which allows those responsible for haze affecting the country to be held legally accountable.
The principle of non-interference should never become a convenient shield for corporate negligence, weak enforcement and environmental destruction.

Punishments must be severe enough to deter future offences. Without transparency, accountability and meaningful penalties, the annual cycle of fires, haze, public anger and official promises will just continue.

The public has run out of patience with agreements, arrangements and endless diplomatic talk. It is time for Asean leaders to show genuine political courage and treat transboundary haze as the serious public health and environmental crisis that it is.
After 24 years of talks, the people of this region deserve more than another statement of concern. We deserve clean air, and we deserve it now.

26af6f271b01258a: SINGAPORE, Sept 24 — A video of a man following a pair of female students and allegedly filming them using his smart glasses has gone viral, sparking safety concerns.
The video was first posted to Reddit by user BBlackjack160 showing a bespectacled man in a grey shirt and black shorts tailing two girls in school uniform through a temporary sheltered walkway.
The girls appear to be unaware of his presence behind them as the person behind the camera walks up towards the man.
He is wearing a mask and clutching his phone to his chest as he presses what seems like a button on his black-rimmed glasses.
He then immediately makes a U-turn and walks in the opposite direction of the girls and the person filming him.
Although the video has been removed by Reddit, several Redditors commented that his actions seemed suspicious.
“He is definitely pressing something,” one commenter alleged with a screenshot from the video.

Another Redditor added that the way the man held his phone in the video “looks like he is recording using that”, referring to how the phone is angled such that it could potentially get a good angle of the two girls.
Netizens have also responded in the thread claiming that they recognise him.
One Redditor alleged that the man hangs out at Junction 8 while waiting for Raffles Institution students to be dismissed around midday.
Another commenter claimed that when she studied at Raffles Junior College, she saw the man waiting outside Marymount MRT station asking her to do a “survey”.
“It was a bunch of really random and weird questions,” she wrote.
Yet another Redditor wrote: “Omg please don’t give him anything! I made a mistake and filled in his stupid survey and months later he contacted me on Telegram.”
Checks by AsiaOne show that the girls’ uniform in the video look similar to that of Raffles Institution students.
“He’s still at it?” wrote a Reddit user, adding that she had reported him “back when Meta glasses did not exist” and he recorded girls with his phone.
But the user said the police could not take any action as he had the right to be there since it was a public area.
“It’s terrible that he is still doing it [after] all these years later. Stay safe and vigilant please, girls!”
In response to AsiaOne’s queries, the police confirmed that a report was lodged and investigations are ongoing. — AsiaOne
1d1c06f499821699: KUALA LUMPUR: Pendang MP Datuk Awang Solahuddin Hashim should publicly explain and apologise for allegations he withdrew against Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, says Amanah vice-president Datuk Mahfuz Omar.
Mahfuz said although Awang had settled the matter in court, he still had a responsibility to explain to voters what happened and why the allegations were withdrawn.
"Awang withdrawing the allegations is okay, but do not let the poison remain in the minds of the people," he said in a statement today.
The suit was settled at the High Court yesterday after Anwar and Awang agreed to the settlement terms.
Anwar withdrew the action without an order as to costs and without liberty to file afresh. A mutually agreed public statement was also submitted to the court.
Mahfuz said Awang should openly explain the matter to voters, express regret and apologise for statements he claimed had influenced public perceptions.

He said MPs had broad scope to criticise the prime minister and government policies, point out weaknesses and expose alleged wrongdoing, but must respect the line between criticism, allegations and defamation.
"Political statements can be withdrawn, but perceptions already planted in people's minds are not so easily withdrawn," he said.
Mahfuz also urged opposition politicians not to make unsubstantiated allegations and then consider the matter settled once the statements were withdrawn.
He said a strong opposition was one that could substantiate its allegations and accept responsibility when it was wrong.
"Politics is not a contest over who can make the strongest allegations. Politics is about who is most responsible towards the truth," he said.
He urged politicians on both sides to treat the episode as a lesson and ensure political differences did not come at the expense of truth.

ff62af4f91cdac90: NAGOYA: Thailand are the latest country to slam the organisation at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan, likening it to a "chaotic" game of "musical chairs".
Athletes have complained of poor accommodation, long delays at airports and in boarding cruise ship housing.
Erratic transport services have seen competitors' buses to training and venues turning up late, or in some cases not at all.
The continent's biggest sporting showpiece, with more than 17,000 athletes and officials, has faced multiple issues during its first full week.
Some teams said there was a shortage of rooms, while others complained about the quality of accommodation provided by organisers.

No traditional athletes' village has been built as a cost-cutting measure, with participants instead staying in temporary container-style huts, hotels and the Costa Serena cruise ship moored in Nagoya port.
"It remains a problem, from the beginning until now," Chalitrat Chandrubeksa, deputy secretary general of the National Olympic Committee of Thailand, told AFP late on Wednesday.
"The number of (rooms available on) cruise ships and hotels does not match our actual number of athletes," he added.
"On the peak day, we required 201 beds on the cruise ship but they provided only 170.

"When athletes checked in and found their names missing from the list, they had to be placed somewhere else and when the new athletes arrived, the previous ones had to move out and look for other hotels.
"It's like musical chairs."
Frustrated athletes have made their feelings known online, with complaints also about some of the food.
More than 4,000 people are staying on the ship in Nagoya's port and 2,000 in the cramped wooden container huts, called "villas" by the organisers without a hint of irony.
"We are solving the problem by finding replacement accommodations ourselves," said Chalitrat.
"We had to book our own and make advanced payments for food out of our pockets."
The shortages have meant the Thailand team having to put some staff far away from the games epicentre in the city of Nagoya.
"Our medical team has to stay about one hour 30 minutes from Nagoya.
"We had to rent additional vehicles from Tokyo so they could travel to look after the athletes.
"It has been chaotic.
"We just hope to fulfil and complete this mission as successfully as possible."
Games organisers said Thursday they were working constantly to improve services for athletes.
"We have already increased shuttle buses as much as possible to satisfy athletes' needs," Asian Games organising committee spokesman Hiroshi Koshizuka told AFP on Thursday.
He admitted issues with transport had occurred but said "there had been no significant impact on the Games and no event has been delayed".
"We have set up a system to respond to complaints and we will address them in a sincere manner going forward."

172ccaf7c5e62b48: TANJUNG MALIM: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has given Melaka BN chief Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh the mandate to negotiate with political parties on cooperation ahead of the state election.
Zahid said Rauf, together with officials from the Melaka BN office, would hold discussions and negotiations with any coalition or political party interested in forging an understanding with BN.

He said the outcome of the negotiations would be brought before the BN and Umno leadership at the central level before a final decision was made.

"I, together with my colleagues in the BN Supreme Council and Umno leadership, will make the final decision after the negotiations and discussions have been conducted by the Melaka BN chairman," he said.
Zahid was responding to questions on BN's preparations for the Melaka election following the dissolution of the Legislative Assembly.
The 28-seat Melaka Legislative Assembly was dissolved yesterday, paving the way for the election.
In the 15th Melaka election on Nov 20, 2021, BN formed thee government after winning 21 of the 28 seats, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) won five seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two.
However, the state executive council also included PH assemblymen, reflecting the composition of the unity government at the federal level.
30960304e5fcafa8: TANJUNG MALIM: The Registrar of Societies (RoS) "did not act arbitrarily" in suspending all activities of Perikatan Nasional (PN), as the decision was based on a complaint lodged by one of the coalition's component parties.

fa2106061fd7884e: ISTANBUL, Sept 24 — This year’s El Nino could cause an estimated 451,000 additional deaths from extreme heat worldwide in the first half of the climate pattern, according to a University of Chicago report released yesterday.
The mortality projections cover the period from June 2026, when the current El Nino began, through February 2027, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
The Climate Impact Lab estimates the number of extremely hot days could rise by 44 per cent compared with normal years, with the heaviest toll expected in countries with fewer resources to adapt.

The Sahel region is projected to record 66,800 additional heat deaths from September through February. Southeast Asia could see nearly 39,000 additional deaths, while India and Brazil are projected to record 15,800 and 13,300, respectively.

“This is such a large number that it can be numbing, but it is made up of parents and children, grandparents and neighbours, people going to work, caring for families, and living their lives,” says Michael Greenstone, a co-founder of the Climate Impact Lab

Researchers said tens of thousands of deaths could be prevented through targeted emergency response and resilience measures, including early-warning systems, cooling centres and protections for outdoor workers.
They said reducing deaths from extreme temperatures should be central to preparations for El Nino, alongside efforts to address food security risks.
The report described the current El Nino as a “postcard from our future,” saying it is bringing temperatures similar to what could become normal in about 20 years without greater adaptation.

“Increasing emergency response and better targeting our efforts can save many lives this year. But 20 years from now, once today’s extreme temperatures become the new normal, we don’t want to be in a constant state of emergency,” said Tamma Carleton, the Climate Impact Lab’s faculty head of research, urging preparation and resources to prepare for the future.
Researchers said they will update the death projections as El Nino develops.
The World Meteorological Organisation has also warned that the current El Nino could become the strongest on record. — Bernama-Anadolu

638617c50bd1be00: HONG KONG: Asian markets were mixed on Thursday as traders eyed a high-stakes summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping set to focus on AI, trade and the Middle East war.
Xi's arrival in Washington coincided with US Treasury Scott Bessent announcing that the superpowers had agreed to extend a trade truce by two months.
The simmering trade war between the world's top two economies is a key concern: while both sides have maintained a tariff truce for nearly a year, they have yet to secure a lasting agreement.
The "economic detente" will now extend beyond its Nov 10 deadline to Jan 10, Bessent said.
But hopes of business deals have been dimmed by the fact that there are no Chinese CEOs in Xi's delegation, two sources told AFP.
In contrast, top US tech bosses including the leaders of major AI companies are set to attend Thursday's banquet.

Pre-summit talks between Bessent and his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng included discussion of creating a communication channel for AI concerns, as warnings swirled that the technology risks wiping out humanity.

"Market participants are looking for signs of cooperation (however feigned) in managing the risks of AI without raising the regulatory risk to the space," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.
Hong Kong, Shanghai and Taipei were in the red, while South Korea's tech-heavy Kospi was closed for a holiday.
Japan's Nikkei was 1.6 per cent up as it reopened after a three-day break.
Tokyo's gains came as the benchmark 10-year JGB yield rose to 3.055 per cent, hitting a 30 year high, after US bond yields jumped.
The benchmark US 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.11 per cent -- its highest level since 2007.
The US Federal Reserve lifted borrowing costs last week, providing relief to traders concerned that policymakers were not moving quickly enough to address a spike in inflation.

The Iran war will be also on the agenda at US-China talks in Washington, Trump confirmed, despite having earlier played down reports that Beijing was supplying Tehran with intelligence as the conflict drags on.
Oil prices cooled off on Thursday after jumping sharply as world leaders at the UN General Assembly offered little to suggest progress in ending the turmoil in the Middle East.
The international benchmark, Brent crude, was down one per cent in early Asian trade after soaring more than three per cent the previous day.
Hopes for a deal to get Gulf oil and gas flowing freely through the Strait of Hormuz as global leaders gathered in New York had sent oil prices down in recent sessions.

f6fad453b0cdb1b6: A few months ago, researchers from the MIT Senseable City Lab published a study about pollution in New York City featuring some new methods. For instance: With machine learning, they identified the types of vehicles appearing in 331 traffic cameras in the city, and estimated the emissions coming from each automobile. Given enough cameras, these visual artificial intelligence techniques could monitor emissions with an unprecedented combination of precision and scale.  For that matter, visual AI today can address all kinds of questions for urban planners. Why exactly is traffic snarling? What are the most dangerous aspects of different intersections? Which parts of plazas or parks attract the most people? Across cities, more images means more data, more insight — and more concerns about privacy and fairness.  “We can treat these digital images as data and quantify features of the city,” says Fábio Duarte, an MIT researcher and co-author of a new book about visual AI and urban studies. “With computer vision techniques, each image is a dataset.” Still, he adds, “We have to be careful about it.”  And while urbanists have long used visual analysis to inform their thinking, now it’s possible to an unprecedented extent.  “Everybody has been observing the urban environment and trying to get some insight,” says Martina Mazzarello, an MIT scholar and a co-author of the new book. “But what if we can do that at a large scale and get some insight everywhere?” The scholars explore these topics in “How AI Sees the City: Urban Visual Intelligence,” published this month by Routledge. The authors are Duarte, a principal research scientist and associate director of the MIT Senseable City Lab; Mazzarello, a research scientist and lead of MIT Senseable City Lab global initiatives; Carlo Ratti, a professor of the practice and founder and director of the MIT Senseable City Lab; and Fan Zhang, an assistant professor at the Institute of Remote Sensing and GIS at Peking University. “Great urbanists such as Kevin Lynch and Willian H. Whyte showed us the extraordinary value of ‘looking’ at the city,” Ratti says, referring to two prominent thinkers about city dynamics whose work is described in the book. “Today, visual AI gives us new ways to build on that tradition — allowing us to observe cities at a scale and with a level of detail that was previously impossible.”  New tool, long tradition “How AI Sees the City” stems from the work of the MIT Senseable City Lab, founded in 2004, which uses data to better understand urban dynamics. As the authors discuss in the book, there is a long history of visual representations that shape the way we think about cities, from Romans building marble maps to the introduction of photography — which produced influential urban images about things like Hausmann’s reshaping of Paris or the crowding of tenements in New York City’s Lower East Side during the 19th century. More recently, some scholars have used visual studies to better understand city form, including Lynch, a former MIT professor whose 1960 book, “The Image of the City,” influenced many scholars. Whyte, a sociologist famous for his book “The Organization Man,” then became an urbanist closely examining public spaces. By explicitly placing AI in a continuum with these visual urban studies, the authors are making a point: Powerful as it might be, we can still think of AI primarily as a tool serving human purposes, as we seek to design and refine urban form. “Kevin Lynch at MIT was only using paper and pen,” Duarte says. “We can now scale up what he was doing, with visual AI, while also looking at many different dimension of cities.”  There are extensive possibilities for applying visual AI to urban planning, ranging from emissions to traffic flow, safety, better imagery of street-level activity and sidewalks, and much more. The book also examines, for instance, urban greenery. While satellite imagery can show us how much tree cover and green spaces cities have, near-ubiquitous images from phones and other sources can also reveal to what extent people glimpse greenery in everyday life, a factor in reported wellness. “The real promise of visual AI is not simply that computers can look at millions of images,” Zhang says. “It is that we can connect what is visible in those images — streets, buildings, greenery, traffic, public space — with larger questions about how cities function and how people experience them.” Better image recognition by AI even extends to urban interiors. By using images from 400,000 AirBnB listings across the world, one recent Senseable City study shows that, contrary to some claims, interior design styles are not becoming globally more homogeneous, but reflect significant geographic differences.  “No matter what it is, we can learn from what we can see and then use it as urban designers, planners, policymakers, and citizens,” Mazzarello says. “It can be our eyes, or cameras with computers, but in the end it’s the same methodology, and now we are trying to optimize the ways we can use these tools.” Promise and pitfalls If the promise of visual AI for urban studies is vast, the pitfalls are concerning. In “How AI Sees the City,” the authors outline multiple potential problems with the technology, including the intrusiveness of widespread visual surveillance and the potential for bias being reinforced through AI systems.  The installation of ubiquitous cameras can quickly raise concerns about surveillance. London, an early adopter of CCTV, has about 210 cameras per square mile. But eight of the world’s 10 most camera-heavy cities are in China; Shanghai has over 5,000 cameras per square mile. Such surveillance practices have raised controversy in other parts of the world, with debate over the uses of traffic cameras bubbling up in the U.S. this year as well.  In evaluating the potential safety gains from intensive video recording, the authors write, “the benefits must be weighed against the significant erosion of personal freedom and the potential for abuse inherent in a system of constant monitoring.” Meanwhile, AI systems can reinforce social biases as well, leading to the production of data that reinforce prior perceptions as much as underlying realities — about people, neighborhoods, and whole cities. If AI models are trained on majority population groups, they may not evaluate minority groups the same way.  “We need to teach AI to see, and depending on how you teach it, it will see what what is embedded in the culture,” Duarte says. “AI is not neutral.” Still, as Mazzarello adds, “our eyes are not neutral, either. Every tool has to be guided in the right way, and trained in the best way.”  Other scholars have praised “How AI Sees the City.” Michael Batty of University College London has called it a “fascinating book” that “shows how we are beginning to interpret the world of urban design, suggesting ways in which we might improve design using urban analytics, AI and large language models.” Ultimately, though the authors think there is great value in deploying visual AI to learn more about our cities, how they function, and how they might be improved. With caution and independent thinking, progress is possible. Or, as they conclude in the book, “We should explore this wisely, critically, and creatively.”
ba446e502b95d95c: SYDNEY: For decades, whenever house prices in Australia fell, the central bank rode to the rescue with rate cuts to shore up economic demand and keep households spending.
House prices are falling once again, but this time the central bank is raising rates, potentially subjecting the housing market to its worst downturn in a generation.

The Reserve Bank of Australia is expected to lift interest rates for a fourth time next Tuesday to a 15-year high of 4.6 per cent, according to market participants and nearly all of the economists polled by Reuters.

An overseas war is complicating the near-term inflation outlook, a global investment boom in data centres is adding to domestic demand for goods and services and government spending on defence and healthcare appears set to stay elevated, lifting longer-term borrowing costs worldwide, economists say.

"I think we're moving into a new world," Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock said on Tuesday, contrasting the situation with an era of free and open trade and low inflation, when the bank's job was to manage demand.
"These shocks to the supply side of the economy are very difficult for monetary policy to deal with."
As a result, inflation will stay high for longer than a typical downturn would suggest, meaning falling housing prices will not be sufficient on their own to push the RBA to cut rates.

While many Australians are struggling financially, an unusually resilient labour market is supporting incomes, leaving households with enough spare cash to splurge on electric vehicles as oil prices surge.
Keeping inflation contained will require higher rates than in the past, said Luke Yeaman, chief economist at the Commonwealth Bank of Australia, which expects a hike next week.
"This means the slowing economy will not bring much in the way of immediate or major rate relief for Australian households," he said.
NOT ENOUGH TO MOVE RBA

The RBA has raised interest rates three times this year, taking the cash rate back to its post-pandemic high of 4.35 per cent, which was enough to bring inflation down from a 7.8 per cent peak. Yet heading into next week's meeting, policymakers are debating a critical question: have they done enough this time?

The housing market suggests tightening is already biting, with national prices down nearly four per cent from their peaks, a fall compounded by a government tax change on investment properties that has hobbled investor lending.
More economists are tipping a peak-to-trough fall of 10 per cent for housing prices in this cycle, the biggest in three decades. HSBC forecasts 13 per cent if rates rise twice more.

For policymakers, that might still not be enough. Sarah Hunter, an assistant RBA governor, played down the link between falling house prices and household spending. Earlier this month, she said house prices would need to fall by 10 per cent on a sustained basis to have a substantial impact on household spending.
"So no recovery in house prices over a one- to two-year horizon," she said. "That, at least in historical context, would be quite surprising to see."
Markets have taken the hint. Traders are fully pricing a further rise to 4.85 per cent, with a 70 per cent chance of rates reaching 5.1 per cent.
WARS AND DATA CENTRES
When the RBA held policy steady for a second meeting in August, it singled out the US-Israeli war on Iran and the data centre boom as key inflation risks.

Oil prices are back above US$100 a barrel, threatening to feed through into broader price pressures, while RBA Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser recently returned from the US more worried about costs after having seen the AI-driven investment frenzy firsthand.

Much of what is driving activity this year - the data centre boom, fiscal spending and immigration - is not sensitive to interest rates, unlike before the pandemic when households did most of the work, said Lachlan Dynan, macro strategist at Deutsche Bank.
That leaves housing to absorb what the rest of the economy will not.

"You can be bearish on the housing market and still think the RBA is going to hike," Dynan said. "In order to bring the aggregate economy into balance, maybe you need a larger housing downturn than otherwise."

cdeebdc91e39e84c: SYDNEY: Australia's jobless rate unexpectedly rose to a five-year high in August even as employment enjoyed a solid rebound, a mixed report that left markets still wagering on an imminent rate hike to fight inflation.

Markets imply a 95 per cent probability that the Reserve Bank of Australia will raise interest rates a fourth time next Tuesday to 4.6 per cent. The Australian dollar, however, slipped another 0.3 per cent to US$0.7018, a seven-week low after heavy losses overnight.

Net employment rose 39,500 in August from July, when it fell 15,800, data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed on Thursday. That was above market forecasts for a 20,000 increase and driven entirely by part-time roles.

The jobless rate rose to 4.6 per cent, above forecasts for a steady 4.5 per cent and the highest level since late 2021, as the participation rate climbed to 67.1 per cent, up 0.2 percentage point. The ABS said it recorded a higher proportion of people who were previously not in the labour force moving to be unemployed.

"Employment growth failed to keep pace with the influx of people into the labour force in August, easing some of the tightness in the labour market," said Oscar Guth, economist for Oxford Economics Australia.

"Even so, inflation pressures extend well beyond the labour market, with oil above USUS$100 a barrel and trimmed mean inflation stuck at 3.6 per cent in July," said Guth, adding that he expected the RBA to hike next Tuesday.

For August, the labour force rose 67,700, up 2.1 per cent from a year earlier, while employment rose a slower 1.6 per cent, suggesting the labour market is gradually loosening. That is consistent with the RBA's judgement that the labour market has eased a little but remains tight.
Governor Michele Bullock said this week that unemployment in a range of 4.5 per cent to 5.0 per cent could help restrain inflation, suggesting some rise might be needed from here.

The central bank has raised interest rates three times this year to 4.35 per cent to tame inflation, matching a post-pandemic high. Yet core inflation is still running at 3.6 per cent, well above the RBA's target range of two per cent to three per cent.

Bullock has warned inflation risks are materialising off the back of the Middle East conflict and a data centre investment boom. With oil back above US$100 a barrel, markets have sharply repriced the global rate outlook, with Australia's cash rate now seen peaking near 5.0 per cent.
9f3b776565206266: KUALA LUMPUR: Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd's dividend outlook remains intact despite higher bond yields, with the potential earnings impact from its fixed-income securities expected to be limited.

Kenanga Research estimated that higher bond yields in the third quarter of calendar year 2026 could have a one per cent impact on earnings from fixed-income securities classified as fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL).

However, the firm said the impact should be relatively small compared with other banks as about 98 per cent of fixed income securities requiring marked-to-market are found in the fair value through other comprehensive income (FVOCI) category (revalued through reserves).

"Based on CET1 levels of 13.4 per cent, our calculation indicates that the rise in Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) rates (at a 50 basis points (bps) since June for 10-year MGS), could still allow CET1 to remain comfortably above 13 per cent, ie. not seeing dividends risk."
The bank also has an additional 60-70 bps capital benefit from the adoption of Basel three final reforms, it added.

Kenanga Research said Alliance Bank's deposit competition remains, though this also reflects a favourable loan pipeline, with the competition levels still commensurate with previously revised net interest margin (NIM) guidance.
It noticed that the bank's loan to fund ratio was at 87.7 per cent as at end-June which has headroom versus the industry's 82.3 per cent.
"We believe this ratio could nudge closer to the industry average as it increasingly taps short-term wholesale funding, which could be less pricey versus promotional fixed deposit rates," it said.
Overall, Kenanga Research said Alliance Bank's smaller exposure to fixed income investment securities exposed to profit and loss revaluation confers a higher degree of earnings protection near term.
"Alliance Bank also is also viewed as an expanded FBM KLCI inclusion candidate."
The firm kept its "Outperform" call in Alliance Bank with target price of RM5.50 for its small-cap bank pick.

89742006fa11c0dd: KOTA BARU: A 10-year-old girl has died after she was run over by a lorry while riding pillion on a motorcycle in Kubang Kerian.
Her mother, Nadja Aida Natasha Mohd Noor, 30, said Putri Nur Aishah Abdullah was pronounced dead on Monday.
She said the incident occurred on Sunday when Putri Nur Aishah was riding with her grandfather, Bakri Daud, 61, on their way home to Kampung Chicha after having a meal together.
Nadja said their motorcycle brushed against a lorry travelling in the same direction.
"My father fell to the left and suffered only minor injuries, while my daughter fell to the right and was run over by the lorry," she said.
She said her daughter was taken to Hospital Pakar Universiti Sains Malaysia, Kubang Kerian, and was in critical condition after suffering severe bleeding.
Doctors performed emergency surgery to insert metal plates into her pelvis to help stop the bleeding, she said.
Nadja said her daughter continued to bleed after the surgery, and doctors called her the following day to discuss a second operation.
She said her daughter's heart suddenly stopped for about 15 minutes during the discussion before doctors performed CPR and her pulse returned.
She said her daughter's oxygen level had dropped to about 30 per cent.
Putri Nur Aishah was buried at the Kampung Chicha Muslim Cemetery at 9.30pm on Monday.
Nadja said she had accepted her daughter's death but was disappointed that the lorry driver had not come forward to apologise.
8a225b7388a62c2a: SHAH ALAM, Sept 24 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chief operating officer Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to three counts of graft involving over RM302,000 in home renovation works.
Adi Azuan, 56, claimed trial to all charges after they were read out before Sessions Court Judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud, The Star reported.

According to the charge sheets, Adi Azuan, in his capacity as TH chief operating officer, allegedly accepted gratification for himself in the form of renovation expenses amounting to RM235,866.58, RM50,698.74, and RM15,933.95 for three residential properties at different locations.
He is accused of receiving the works from AG Reka Sdn Bhd director Thamsulazri Ismail, an individual whom the accused knew had official connections with his public duties at the pilgrimage fund.
The offences were allegedly committed on March 7, 2017, at the three properties located in Shah Alam, Kota Damansara, and USJ 2, Subang Jaya.
The charges were framed under Section 165 of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of two years, a fine, or both, upon conviction.

Deputy Public Prosecutor Muaz Ahmad Khairuddin informed the court that the offences were non-bailable, but proposed bail at RM70,000 with one surety should the court exercise its discretion to grant temporary release.
“We leave it to the court’s discretion if it decides to impose additional bail conditions,” Muaz said.

In mitigation, defence counsel Wan Azwan Aiman Wan Fakhruddin appealed for a lower bail sum of RM30,000, stating that his client is the sole provider for four sons aged between 12 and 25 who are still studying, including his eldest who is currently in university. The lawyer also requested that the court not impound Adi Azuan’s passport, contending that he poses no flight risk.
Awang Kerisnada fixed bail at RM50,000 with two sureties and ordered the accused to surrender his passport to the custody of the court.
“If he needs to use his passport, he can write to the court,” Awang Kerisnada said.
The court scheduled the case for mention on Nov 25.
Adi Azuan was originally slated to be charged on Sept 3, but the proceedings were adjourned after he was admitted to hospital to undergo an angiogram procedure.
7d5d09e882ee6783: SHAH ALAM: Former Tabung Haji (TH) chief operating officer (COO) Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani has claimed trial at the sessions court here to three charges of receiving renovation costs totalling RM302,499.27 for three houses nine years ago.
Adi, 56, made the plea before judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud.

All three charges were framed under Section 165 of the Penal Code. The section makes it an offence for a public servant to obtain valuables without consideration. Those found guilty can be jailed for up to two years and fined.
According to the charges, Adi, who was then TH’s COO, received valuable items in the form of renovation costs for three houses from AG Reka Sdn Bhd director Thamsulazri Ismail.

The renovation costs comprised RM235,866.58 for a house in Jalan Polo Air 13/58B, Section 13, Shah Alam; RM50,698.74 for a house in Jalan Sepah Puteri 5/20B, Kota Damansara; and RM15,933.95 for a house in Jalan USJ Heights 2/2A, Subang Jaya.
The offences were allegedly committed on March 7, 2017.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) deputy public prosecutor Muaz Ahmad Khairuddin proposed bail of RM70,000.
However, defence lawyer Wan Azwan Aiman Wan Fakhruddin appealed for the amount to be reduced to RM30,000, saying his client supports four sons aged between 12 and 25 who are still studying.
"My client retired last year and also cooperated with MACC in its investigations in 2018 and last month," he said.
The lawyer also applied for Adi’s passport to be returned as he plans to perform the umrah, adding that Adi requires treatment for a heart condition.

The court granted Adi bail of RM50,000 with two sureties and ordered him to report to the MACC office every three months, surrender his passport to the court and refrain from contacting or interfering with witnesses.
Proceedings against Adi were initially postponed after he was admitted to Universiti Malaya Medical Centre on Aug 31 due to a heart-related condition.
Adi was remanded for four days by MACC in December 2018 to assist investigations into the use of an interior design contractor linked to TH for renovation work at his home.
d57b995f2bc167aa: SEOUL: North Korea will keep its nuclear weapons "forever", its foreign minister vowed Thursday, dismissing the South Korean president's renewed calls for a denuclearised Korean Peninsula.
Pyongyang has legally enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state, with its leadership repeatedly declaring the country's atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible.

The foreign minister's remarks came a day after South Korean President Lee Jae Myung told the UN General Assembly he wanted to halt further growth in Pyongyang's weapons capabilities and eventually achieve a Korean Peninsula "free from nuclear weapons".

"I reaffirm and reconfirm in the strongest tone of voice the steadfast will of our state to keep nuclear weapons through all ages," North Korea's foreign minister Choe Son Hui said in a statement carried by the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).
The country's nuclear status was "irreversible in any case and will remain unchanged forever", she added.
"The coexistence of confrontation and dialogue may be workable for anyone, but they can never be a considerable one for the DPRK," Choe said, using the country's official acronym.
North Korea's status as a nuclear weapons state was "everlasting" regardless of what hostile forces said, she added.

At the UN, Lee -- who has repeatedly sought to revive dialogue with the North -- also said South Korea would "lay the groundwork" for the resumption of long-stalled dialogue between Pyongyang and Washington.
The South Korean president said last week that US President Donald Trump "clearly wants dialogue" with Pyongyang.
Trump, who met the North Korean leader three times during his first term, said last month that he planned to meet Kim Jong Un later this year.
Separately on Thursday, Pyongyang said it had tested "updated 240-millimetre controlled multiple-launch rockets" on Sept 22.
KCNA said the weapons were capable of striking targets up to 115km away.
North Korea's vice foreign minister is expected to address the UN General Assembly next week.
ea5b461ed38f6c6e: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian palm oil futures opened slightly higher on Thursday after four straight sessions of losses, supported by stronger rival Dalian oils and by India's decision to cut import duty.
The gains were limited, however, by weaker Chicago soyoil and lower crude oil prices, which reduced support for palm oil, used both in food and as a biofuel.
The benchmark palm oil contract for December delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange gained RM11, or 0.23 per cent, to RM4,779 (US$1,170.75) a metric ton in early trade.
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract rose 0.22 per cent, while its palm oil contract added 0.47 per cent. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade were down 0.44 per cent.
Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.

Oil prices edged lower, after climbing four per cent in the previous session, as Iran said it remained open to diplomacy to end the US-Iran war, though the two countries remain far apart on ways to do so.
Weaker crude oil futures make palm a less attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
The ringgit, palm's currency of trade, weakened 0.05 per cent against the dollar, making the commodity slightly cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies.

India has cut the basic import duty on crude and refined edible oils, including palm oil, soyoil and sunflower oil, the government said late on Wednesday, as it seeks to lower prices during the peak festive season.
Palm oil may retest support at RM4,732 per ton, a break below which may trigger a fall into the RM4,677 to RM4,711 range, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said.

Debt markets were on edge on Thursday, as Japanese bonds followed Treasuries lower, while Asian equities were mixed as investors weighed simmering Middle East tensions and prospects for talks between the United States and China.
ce35bf6d29fc7597: PETALING JAYA: Puteri Umno Pulau Pinang menggesa Ketua Srikandi PKR, Nurhidayah Che Rose tidak mengalih isu mengenai perubahan syarat ekuiti 30% Bumiputera bagi institusi pendidikan swasta dengan mengaitkannya dengan pentadbiran bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak.

Ketuanya, Ameera Nadia Mohd Shafiee, berkata Nurhidayah perlu menjawab persoalan sebenar berhubung perubahan syarat itu, termasuk mengapa Kementerian Pendidikan (KPM) mengaitkan Kementerian Pelaburan, Perdagangan dan Industri (Miti) dalam perkara tersebut.
“Rujukan kepada pentadbiran terdahulu pada 2009 dan 2012 tidak menjawab persoalan utama yang dibangkitkan ketua penerangan Puteri Umno.
“Jika penyelarasan ini sekadar pelaksanaan dasar 2012, mengapa ia diumumkan sebagai penyelarasan terbaharu,” katanya dalam satu kenyataan.

Beliau menjawab, kenyataan Nurhidayah semalam yang menggesa Ketua Penerangan Puteri Umno Nooryana Najwa Najib merujuk keputusan kerajaan terdahulu pimpinan bapanya sebelum mempertikaikan perubahan syarat ekuiti 30% Bumiputera bagi institusi pendidikan swasta.

Nurhidayah berkata pada April 2009, ketika Najib menjadi perdana menteri, kerajaan mengumumkan liberalisasi 27 subsektor perkhidmatan tanpa syarat ekuiti, sebelum liberalisasi diperluas kepada beberapa subsektor pendidikan tiga tahun kemudian.
Dalam pada itu, Ameera berkata Srikandi PKR juga tidak sepatutnya mengaitkan nama Najib sebagai perisai setiap kali timbul persoalan mengenai keputusan kementerian ketika ini.

Beliau turut menggesa kerajaan menjelaskan sama ada Miti benar-benar terlibat dalam perbincangan itu dan sama ada Kementerian Ekonomi dirujuk serta pihak yang membuat dan meluluskan keputusan tersebut.
“Jangan alihkan isu kepada tahun 2009 dan 2012. Jawab dahulu apa yang berlaku pada 2026.
“Rakyat berhak mengetahui siapa yang membuat keputusan, siapa yang dirujuk dan asas penyelarasan tersebut,” katanya.

Kelmarin, Nooryana dilaporkan berkata KPM perlu segera memperbetul rekod dan menjelaskan mengapa Miti dikaitkan dengan penyelarasan syarat pegangan 30% ekuiti Bumiputera bagi institusi pendidikan swasta.
Nooryana berkata perkara itu menjadi persoalan selepas Miti menegaskan kementerian itu tidak terlibat dalam penentuan dasar berkenaan.

Miti kelmarin pula berkata pihaknya tidak mempunyai makluman mengenai keputusan KPM memansuhkan syarat itu, sambil menjelaskan dasar pemilikan ekuiti Bumiputera adalah di bawah bidang kuasa Unit Perancang Ekonomi (EPU), Kementerian Ekonomi.
d35621768dd1bbe2: KUALA LUMPUR: Hamzah Zainudin, the long-time political operator who helped two prime ministers to power, could again have a hand in shaping who governs as he pushes the nation’s two biggest parties towards an alliance.
Since launching Parti Wawasan Negara in June, Hamzah has become the official parliamentary opposition leader thanks to the backing of the largest rival group, PAS.
His self-professed goal is to push PAS into a national alliance with Umno, consolidating the two chief parties representing Malay Muslims who make up almost 60% of the population.

If realised, such a pact could undermine Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s coalition government, which has counted Umno as a partner since an inconclusive 2022 election. It would also create a formidable political alliance going into the next polls, which must be held by early 2028.
"What I’m trying to pump into their heads is: 'Hey you’re Malays, sit down'," Hamzah said in a Sept 17 interview at his office in Bukit Tunku, Kuala Lumpur.
"In this country the Malays are the majority and if the Malays are not united, how can a country be stable?"

Umno and PAS successfully cooperated in the August state election in Negeri Sembilan, where they agreed not to field candidates against each other and ended up ousting Anwar’s Pakatan Harapan (PH) from the state government. They’re now considering a similar arrangement in Melaka, where another state election is due within the next two months.

While Hamzah said he played a role in bringing Umno and PAS together, he played down their need for him now as an intermediary. Leaders of both groups have attended each other’s recent party gatherings, with both sides publicly expressing interest in extending their cooperation nationally.
That has upset Anwar, with people familiar with the matter saying his relationship with deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has deteriorated.
Zahid, who leads Umno, wants a national election to be held "as soon as possible" in a sign Umno wants out of its pact with Anwar’s PH.

Malaysia’s complex political system aims to ensure representation along with economic and other privileges for Malay Muslims, who have accounted for all the country’s prime ministers since independence in 1957. At the same time, governing coalitions traditionally provide a voice for the country’s ethnic Chinese, Indians and other minorities.

Hamzah, who began his political career with Umno and whose Wawasan is now allied with PAS, remains well positioned to help bridge divisions between the two parties that have spent years competing for the same Malay Muslim voters.

The 69-year-old played a key role in gathering the parliamentary support that propelled Muhyiddin Yassin to the top office in 2020, including winning the backing of Umno and PAS. That brought down the government of Dr Mahathir Mohamad, who acknowledged Hamzah’s role in getting the two big Malay parties to cooperate.
Muhyiddin then named Hamzah secretary-general of Bersatu.
When Muhyiddin lost his parliamentary majority just a year later, Hamzah helped rally support for Ismail Sabri Yaakob to become the next prime minister.

A fresh, national electoral pact formed by the main Malay parties remains possible, according to Syaza Shukri, an associate professor of political science at International Islamic University Malaysia. But the Muhyiddin administration was beset by infighting, and Umno’s Malay nationalism has long put it at odds with PAS’s more explicitly Islamist vision of government.
"Political Malay unity is difficult because every party is looking out for itself," Syaza said.
Hamzah was expelled from Muhyiddin’s Bersatu in February following a protracted power struggle.

He says his barely three-month-old Wawasan party has attracted more than 50,000 members, and forecasts those numbers could reach 300,000 by the end of the year. By comparison, Umno has about 3.5 million members, while Anwar’s PKR claims about one million.

Wawasan made its electoral debut less than a month after its formal registration, winning three assembly seats in Negeri Sembilan. Hamzah confirmed the party will also contest the Melaka election. Unlike other Malay parties, it allows other ethnicities to be ordinary members and hold leadership positions, while reserving the presidency for Malays.
"I’m not new in this game," Hamzah said. "I was actually a businessman before I really turned to politics."
Hamzah won his parliamentary seat in 2008 under Umno, but quit the party after the 1MDB scandal led to Umno’s first-ever national defeat in 2018.
He joined Bersatu, having been convinced to remain in politics by the late tycoon and former finance minister Daim Zainuddin, who helped draw Hamzah into politics in the early 2000s.

He views PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang, an Islamic scholar, as a "guru", and their relationship led to the Islamic party announcing in June that Hamzah would return as opposition leader, with PAS leader Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar remaining chairman of the Perikatan Nasional opposition bloc.
Hamzah is the "only one that can talk to both Zahid and Hadi", Syaza said. "I wouldn’t even be surprised if he becomes the PM candidate."
Hamzah dismissed any suggestion he’s positioning himself to become the prime minister, saying larger parties have potential candidates like PAS’s Samsuri and Umno’s Zahid.
"I will help anyone who aspires to be the prime minister," Hamzah said, arguing he can help assemble the people and alliances required to govern. "You have heard people describe me as an operator."
But the one alliance Hamzah does rule out is with Anwar.
"I’m an opposition leader and Anwar is the prime minister," he said. "He doesn’t want me and I do not want him."
1aa8ee00a87621f5: SAN FRANCISCO, Sept 24 — Meta unveiled several new wearables powered by its AI models yesterday, including an audio-only, camera-free version of its smart glasses, amid global concerns about privacy and the filming of women and girls without their consent.

CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced the new lineup of glasses at the social media giant’s annual Connect conference at its Menlo Park headquarters, where he also touted the company’s new personal artificial intelligence assistant, Muse.

“There are almost 2 billion people in the world who wear glasses today... and we think that in the coming years, most of these are going to get upgraded to AI glasses,” Zuckerberg told the audience of developers and executives.
Muse will be “the centrepiece of our vision,” Zuckerberg said.

The audio-only glasses will ship on October 13 and start at US$349 (RM1,424). They arrive amid growing questions worldwide about privacy violations from tiny cameras on glasses and other wearables, which critics have dubbed “pervert” glasses.
Smart glasses let wearers take photos, film videos, listen to music, make phone calls, translate text or interact with an AI assistant.
The audio-only versions will complement the release of dozens of new smart glasses models that keep the photo and video filming option.
Building in privacy features such as a recording indicator light is “really important,” Meta’s vice president of AI product, Vishal Shah, told AFP yesterday.
“We wanted people to clearly understand that this was something that was recording, and we’ve only made that light more explicit over time,” Shah said.
“We said a lot about that when the glasses first launched, and I think we probably need to keep repeating that more than we have been more recently because none of that’s changed,” he added.
With nearly four billion monthly active users across its ecosystem, Meta is betting that wearables like smart glasses can become an easy entry point for people to use its AI software.
Meta launched its first smart glasses in 2021, and last year unveiled “display” glasses that project images onto the lens.
Earlier this year, the company released its own Meta-branded AI glasses, separate from its partnership with eyewear maker EssilorLuxottica, which produces several Ray-Ban and Oakley Meta models.

Meta also announced several new styles of its flagship Meta Ray-Ban glasses. The display version, priced from US$799, will soon be available in new markets including Britain, France, Italy, Germany and Canada.
The company will also soon launch mixed reality glasses that are much lighter than its earlier Quest VR headsets.
Called Meta VR Glasses, they are powered by an external battery and memory pack tethered by a cord, allowing the headset itself to be lighter.
Zuckerberg said the glasses weigh about as much as a deck of cards.
They have no external controls, relying instead on hand gestures and voice commands.
The VR Glasses will launch in spring 2027 for US$1,299.
Meta Muse
Meta has spent billions of dollars to stay competitive in AI but faces pushback on multiple fronts.
The glasses are designed to work with Muse, the company’s first agentic app for consumers. It performs tasks on users’ behalf like a digital personal assistant.
After connecting personal accounts — for finance, health and shopping — users can ask Muse to sign up for services, book appointments and make calls.
The Muse app became the top free app in the Google Play Store and Apple App Store, overtaking OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude and Google’s Gemini.
Zuckerberg teased another product on Wednesday, the Muse Charm, that will ship ahead of the holidays this year; Meta did not provide a price.
The “charm” is a small, puck-like device with a display that will allow users to interact with their Muse agent separately from a smartphone.

Amazon this week blocked Meta from using AI bots to shop automatically for users, while Instacart, Shopify and Expedia have announced partnerships to integrate their services into Muse. Meta said Walmart, Best Buy, Gap and Sephora are also partnering with the app.
Meta, which earns most of its revenue from ads on Instagram and Facebook, faces mounting child safety and privacy challenges worldwide.

In August, it settled a lawsuit brought by US states accusing it of violating consumer protection and children’s online privacy laws, agreeing to pay up to US$18 billion and impose restrictions for teenagers.
The company also faces age-based restrictions and bans abroad, as well as thousands of potential personal injury suits in the US. — AFP
